steps.content: Your eyes snap open. You are lying on your back, still surrounded by darkness, but the fire and the scorch marks are gone. Only the sensation remains, your back, the back of your head, and the shackles on your hands are all burning with pain.
But the mental chaos has subsided, and you can't help but reach into your pocket—the blue Hypercube fragment is there.
The shackles are responsive, and that... was not a dream, but an omen, a revelation. You've seen the lava-like scorch marks, the very source of the contamination you're chasing.
Whatever induced BR-004's anomaly stopped here.
But where is here?

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: You're finally awake.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: Shh, don't talk, and don't move. Check your surroundings first. Is there anyone else around?

You calm down, hold your breath and try to perceive your surroundings... You are trapped in a small rectangular space, and with the help of a shimmering light falling from above, you can tell it is not very high.

You can feel your heart beating, thump, thump... About a minute passes by, and through that gap occasionally comes the sound of airflow, as clearly audible as your heartbeat... This place is quiet, dim, and cold inside and out.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: There doesn't seem to be anyone else around, so you're safe.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: How are you feeling? I heard that the Chief is not in good physical condition lately. The suspended animation lasted 2 hours, and there could be side effects.

Indeed, the places where the "bullets" hit still hurt a little. You thought they would crack your bones, but now it seems... fine. Except for the fake plasma on your clothes, that feels a little nasty.
You recall the scene where he "shot" you in front of everyone.

steps.speaker: Choice
options: I'm surprised no one saw through your little trick.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: Don't underestimate the little toys of an agent. It was quite shocking to see your head explode, plus the reaction of the two Sinners there...

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: Don't worry. No one will suspect a thing. That Hecate girl almost blew me away through the cage. It doesn't get any better than that. Though it was a bit of a struggle to save them after that.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: Anyway, the plan went well, Chief, and you have now infiltrated the funeral home at the bottom of the Drifter Camp. Your Sinners are also on their way here.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: As long as they can reunite with you before you are pushed into the crematorium, there won't be a problem, probably.
Back in the car...

steps.speaker: Choice
options: Is there a way to infiltrate the place and investigate?

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: The risk is high, but there is indeed a way.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: There is a private funeral home at the bottom of the Drifter Camp. Regardless of your stand, faction, Maniac or not... as long as you die in the territory of the Drifter Camp, you will be taken in and buried.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: Yes, if, unfortunately, there happens to be a conflict, just play it out in front of them. I can meet you halfway.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: As long as I can stop your vital signs on the spot, they won't do anything more to you. Your body already belongs to the funeral home.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Sounds good. I'm already familiar with kidnapping plays. Guess it will be fun to try a new script this time.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: Oh, right, please keep this a secret from your adjutant.
Now, feeling your sore muscles, you regret not spending more time blending in with a disguise.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: Well, the enemies of the Drifter Camp are thinking of the same thing. They've caught several "acting personnel" and tightened up entrance checks recently, so it's not so easy to go undercover.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: Well... the risk has indeed increased. So I'll be keeping a low profile from here, and there will be very little help I can give you.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: Don't try to find me, either. Any "agreement" between you and me will only increase the risk of exposure.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: Haha, sorry, it's not that serious. I have already taken care of everything that should be done, and there will be more suitable people to assist you in the investigation in Drifter Camp. I will step in if it's really necessary.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: Now that you've entered the Drifter Camp, have you sensed anything about the "Corpus"?

steps.speaker: Choice
options: It's been here but has left.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: The shackles are very sensitive to their presence, but now it's calm. Parma and his inheritance are no longer in Drifter Camp.
I don't know if this is a good or bad thing.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: It's a good thing. The population density here is so high, and it will be hard to control the situation. We can relax for a while, at least.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: Take this as a starting point and continue the investigation. You can still find out what "the thing" did here and what Parma did.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: Someone will be along shortly to assist you, but be careful. The attack just now was aimed at you, and they seemed to know you well.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: I'm not sure where the info is from, but it will be used against you. Remember, from now on, do not reveal your identity or the fact that you are still alive.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: Drifter Camp may not be your enemy, but they're definitely not your friend.
It reminds you of the conflict you just had, the gun pointed at the young man and his frantic and cold eyes behind it. Although the plan was already in place, you really faltered at that moment.

steps.speaker: Choice
options: You arrived just in time. Thank you.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: I wanted to see what your fantastic plan was, but there wasn't enough time. When you were hesitating, someone else had already raised a gun and aimed at the back of your head.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: No. You'd have fallen for their trap if you had shot the kid. The relationship with Drifter Camp would be entirely down the drain, and the Syndicate would face a new riot... Your patience was remarkable...

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: It's just you may be used to more surreal battles that are more direct and brutal, but combat with humans is a whole other level of dangerous.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: You have to get used to the cruelty in reality.

steps.speaker: Choice
options: Do you think I made the wrong choice?

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: ...There aren't any right or wrong choices for many things, Chief. Make your choice and keep walking. You can't stop, even if there are sacrifices.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: And the final destination you reach will determine whether the price paid along the way is worth it.
The communication is cut, and you're back in the dark. You can feel the Sinners getting closer on the other end of the shackles, but they will probably take a while.
Before that, you struggle to raise your hand and push the wooden board covering you.
The board wouldn't budge.
Are you too weak after the suspended animation? Or is the wooden box nailed shut?
The corners can be lifted, and you realize that something heavy is pressed into the center of the board.
Is it another wooden box? Many gangsters must have died in that fight just now. It's not too heavy, but you really don't have the strength now, so you decide to lie there and rest.
Instead of making a scene, it's safer to wait for your strength to return or for the Sinners to follow the shackles and find you.
As you ponder, a soft laugh comes from above the wooden box.
Hehe... Giving up so soon?
Someone is out there?!
Oh? Holding your breath again? Aren't you the one talking big, faking your own death just now?
Come one. Make a reasonable offer, and I'll open the lid and resurrect you!
A girl's voice comes from above the board, and you realize she's sitting on it to keep you from getting out. And she's been there since before you woke up!
She must have heard everything you said, and there's no use pretending to be dead. You check for your pistol, but it's not there.

You push again, but nothing happens. Should you try your chance with the Potestas? But without seeing the situation, you could be in trouble if you consume too much of your sanity and there are others outside.
Huh? Where's your offer? Do you want my help or not? You need to work really hard alone to come back from the dead.
Want something to cheer you up?
Before you can react, a shrill sound of an instrument penetrates the board, piercing your eardrums and reaching the depths of your soul.
It's... the sound you heard in the chaos!
